problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=2{y}^{2}\,i+x\,j$ and $C$ is the curve ${y}^{2}=\frac{x-1}{3}$ traversed from the point $A(1,0)$ to the point $B(4,1).$
worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Making $x$ the subject of the equation, we have

$$
{y}^{2}=\frac{x-1}{3}\,⟹\,x=3{y}^{2}+1.
$$

So, the parametrization of the curve is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =(3{t}^{2}+1)\,i+t\,j,\,0\le t\le 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=3{t}^{2}+1,\,y=t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =2{y}^{2}\,i+x\,j \\  & =2{t}^{2}\,i+(3{t}^{2}+1)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}+1)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)j \\  & =6t\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(2{t}^{2}\,i+(3{t}^{2}+1)\,j)\cdot (6t\,i+j) \\  & =2{t}^{2}\cdot 6t+(3{t}^{2}+1)\cdot 1 \\  & =12{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2}+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(12{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2}+1)\,dt \\  & ={[3{t}^{4}+{t}^{3}+t]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =3+1+1-0 \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$
